Null distributions for provider statistics

Source: R/null_models.R
null_models.Rd

A null model gives, for every provider, the mean and standard deviation of the normal distribution its z statistic is referred to: \(z_{adj} = (z - \mathrm{null\_mean}) / \mathrm{null\_sd}\). Three kinds exist: the theoretical null \(N(0, 1)\), a fixed null with values given by the caller (for instance a known scale inflation), and the empirical null estimated robustly from the statistics themselves, overall or within groups of providers of similar size. Any of them can be handed to calibrate(), test() or test_measure().

Usage

null_model(
  kind = c("empirical", "theoretical", "fixed"),
  z = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  n_groups = 4,
  grouping = c("rank", "quantile", "cut"),
  estimator = c("huber", "bisquare", "mm"),
  tuning = NULL,
  maxit = 20,
  acc = 1e-04,
  common_mean = NULL,
  fit_mask = NULL,
  min_group_size = 3,
  small_group = c("error", "theoretical"),
  mean = 0,
  sd = 1
)

Arguments

kind

"empirical" (default), "theoretical" or "fixed".

z

for the empirical null, the provider statistics: a numeric vector, optionally named by provider, or a test result from test() or test_measure(), whose statistic, provider identifiers and (for test()) sizes are used.

size

one size per provider used to form the groups (patients, say); taken from a test result when z is one. Ignored when groups is given.

groups

explicit group label per provider; missing labels get no parameters.

n_groups

number of size groups. Default 4; 1 fits one overall null.

grouping

"rank" (default; the providers sorted by size are dealt into n_groups consecutive blocks of ceiling(n / n_groups), the last block holding the remainder, as the KECC production code for the PPPW and SFR measures and pprof_py do), "quantile" (groups by the empirical quantiles of size, a size equal to a break going to the lower group, as the production SMR and SHR code and EmpiNull do) or "cut" (the sorted providers cut by cut() into n_groups intervals of equal length, the Group_EN of the KECC measures paper).

estimator

robust location-scale estimator of each group, all fitted with MASS::rlm() on an intercept-only model: "huber" (default; Huber's psi with the MAD scale, the production choice), "bisquare" (Tukey's biweight with the MAD scale) or "mm" (MM-estimation: an S-estimate of scale followed by bisquare steps).

tuning

tuning constant of the psi function; MASS defaults 1.345 (Huber) and 4.685 (bisquare).

maxit, acc

iteration limit and convergence tolerance of MASS::rlm() (defaults 20 and 1e-4; EmpiNull's robust calibration uses 1000 and 1e-8 with the bisquare).

common_mean

NULL (default; each group's own fitted location), TRUE (the mean of all eligible statistics) or a number: replaces the groups' locations, the scales are kept as fitted.

fit_mask

logical, one per provider: the providers that enter the fits (TRUE); the others are still calibrated with their group's parameters.

min_group_size

the smallest number of eligible statistics a group may have. Default 3.

small_group

"error" (default) or "theoretical" (a group below min_group_size gets the theoretical null, with a warning).

mean, sd

mean and standard deviation of a fixed null.

Value

An object of class pp_null: a list with kind ("theoretical", "fixed" or "empirical"), mean, sd and group (one per provider for the empirical null, named when the statistics were; single values otherwise), diagnostics (one row per group: group, n_providers, n_fitted, min_size, median_size, max_size, mean_z, sd_z, null_mean, null_sd, converged, n_iter, note) and settings.

References

Efron B (2004). Large-scale simultaneous hypothesis testing: the choice of a null hypothesis. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 99(465), 96-104.

Kalbfleisch JD, Wolfe RA (2013). On monitoring outcomes of medical providers. Statistics in Biosciences, 5, 286-302.

See also

calibrate(), adjust_z()

Examples

d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 40, seed = 1)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_logistic_fe(pd)
tst <- test(fit, statistic = "score", variance = "robust")
nul <- null_model("empirical", tst, n_groups = 2)
nul
#> Empirical null: 2 group(s) by rank, huber estimator
#>  group n_providers n_fitted min_size max_size null_mean null_sd converged
#>      1          20       20       15       39  -0.04996   2.523      TRUE
#>      2          20       20       42       60   0.11395   2.741      TRUE
head(calibrate(tst, nul))
#> Provider tests: score statistic, robust variance (modified); null median = -0.965; two.sided, level 0.95
#>   6 providers: 0 above, 0 below, 6 not different, 0 not tested
#>  provider estimate se null_value statistic z_adjusted null_mean null_sd
#>      P001  -0.7418 NA     -0.965    0.4921     0.2148  -0.04996   2.523
#>      P002  -0.3816 NA     -0.965    2.8172     0.9860   0.11395   2.741
#>      P003  -1.7131 NA     -0.965   -2.1481    -0.8315  -0.04996   2.523
#>      P004  -1.9726 NA     -0.965   -3.7949    -1.4258   0.11395   2.741
#>      P005  -1.5766 NA     -0.965   -2.8597    -1.1135  -0.04996   2.523
#>      P006  -0.6088 NA     -0.965    1.8824     0.6451   0.11395   2.741
#>  null_group      p flag lower upper
#>           1 0.8299    0    NA    NA
#>           2 0.3241    0    NA    NA
#>           1 0.4057    0    NA    NA
#>           2 0.1539    0    NA    NA
#>           1 0.2655    0    NA    NA
#>           2 0.5189    0    NA    NA
